t: The first great steppe empire of eastern Eurasia, the Xiongnu confederation dominated Mongolia from about 209 BCE.
For decades it forced Han China to pay tribute in silk and princesses; its decimal army and court became the model for later steppe empires.
Han campaigns, natural disasters and rival chanyu split it in 48 CE; the Northern Xiongnu vanished as a power around 91 CE.
dyk: In 200 BCE the Xiongnu trapped the Han founder, Emperor Gaozu, for seven days at Baideng; he escaped only after his envoys bribed the chanyu's consort.
ev: Modu seizes power from his father Touman and unites the Xiongnu
Modu surrounds Han Emperor Gaozu for seven days at the Battle of Baideng
The Han accept the heqin treaty of gifts and royal brides in exchange for peace
A failed Han ambush at Mayi ends the policy of appeasement
Wei Qing and Huo Qubing defeat the Xiongnu at the Battle of Mobei
Chanyu Huhanye travels to Chang'an and acknowledges Han overlordship
The confederation splits into Southern and Northern Xiongnu
The Northern Xiongnu suffer a crushing defeat by Han forces and their allies
